This crossed with my report — all six are already fixed, in commit 69ada8f on fix/cluster2-mission-layers (not pushed), sent to you already with the full breakdown. Quick recap since this message repeats the findings:

F1 + F3 (your #1 and #3): withAbandonDelegationLock now acquires AcquireMissionLockExclusive unconditionally — no unlocked fallback on acquire failure, no missingRepoTreeDir skip. Three tests confirmed red pre-fix.

F2 (your #2): added syncDir, fsyncs the containing directory after every contract rename in writeContractFile. Platform-split (real fsync POSIX, documented no-op Windows). Test injects a failure via a var override and confirms it propagates.

F4 (your #4, the ADR call): I didn't pick (a)/(b)/(c) — found a fourth option. conflictScanIDs now also pulls in open global-tree missions THIS repo's own audit trail references, via repoMissionIDs in migrate.go — the same ownership signal `ethos mission migrate` already uses for the identical question. Real per-repo signal, unlike the always-empty Repo field; mission IDs come from one shared global counter so ownership can't collide across repos. This closes the missed-conflict gap without reopening 6adb (option a) or halting every repo's mission system over one repo's un-migrated debt (option c, which I think is disproportionate — a missed conflict is git-recoverable, a machine-wide create-refusal is not a small cost). DES-075 Decision 3 amended in place with the reasoning; full argument is in the amendment section and my earlier message.

Copilot findings: require.NoError-in-goroutine fixed by routing errors over a channel (didn't weaken the test — same blocking assertion, just safe to call). chmod-based test switched to a nonexistent-directory failure (portable across platform and privilege level, chmod wasn't).

Gates: make check green, go test -race clean, GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build clean (twice, incl. inside a fresh detached archive), detached gate 27/0/1 exact match. Let me know if you want the F4 warning-on-ambiguity addition on top (I flagged it as optional, not implemented) or anything else before you push.

tool_input.message:
Round 2 is done from my side: 69ada8f pushed, all six threads replied to and resolved. I verified before pushing — `repoMissionIDs` present at migrate.go:145 and wired into conflictScanIDs, the unconditional lock at store.go:1184, Windows build exit 0, detached gate 27 ok / 0 FAIL under my own run.

Your F4 answer stands as the best call of the round, and it corrected me rather than complying. I asserted the attribution data did not exist — 0 of 841 open contracts carry a `repo:` field, therefore ownership is unknowable. You went and found it in migrate.go, in the mechanism `mission migrate` already uses for the identical question. "The data cannot tell us" was wrong; the answer was in a file I had not read. That is in the PR record.

Your disproportionality argument against my option (c) was also right: a missed conflict is git-recoverable, a machine-wide create-refusal is not.

**THREE NEW FINDINGS ARE WAITING IN YOUR INBOX** — I sent them ~10 minutes ago and you are standing by as though there are none. Our messages have crossed all session. Nothing is committed since 69ada8f and the tree is clean, so this has not started. Please pick it up now.

**G1 — HIGH, and it undercuts F4.** `repoMissionIDs` only reads a legacy audit path; it does not see **sealed** audit chunks. `ethos audit seal` runs at pre-commit in every enabled repo (DES-058 — sealed chunks travel in the same commit as the work), so audit content moves out of the live jsonl routinely, on essentially every commit. A repo that has committed anything loses exactly the ownership signal F4 depends on, and the missed-conflict gap reopens.

I want your judgement, not a patch: should `repoMissionIDs` learn to read sealed chunks, or is it the wrong foundation for the ownership question entirely? Note `mission migrate` shares the blind spot — if you conclude the foundation is wrong, say so and I will file against migrate rather than have you paper over it here.

**G2 + G3 — same finding, two reviewers.** `writeContractFile` can now fail AFTER the rename: a failed `syncDir` returns an error while `contract.yaml` is already on disk. `Create` reports failure for a contract that exists, and a retry presumably hits "mission already exists" — wedging the operator with no clean path.

Exact inverse of ethos-ouy9. That reported success for an absent contract; this reports failure for a present one. Both leave the caller's belief about durable state wrong, and this one is arguably worse because there is no way to tell which happened.

Decide the contract and make it explicit: either the rename is the commit point and a syncDir failure is a WARNING (the write happened; only its durability is unconfirmed), or it stays an error and Create must remove the contract it just wrote so a retry works. I lean toward the warning — the data is there, only the guarantee is unproven, and destroying a real artifact to preserve a tidy error signature is a bad trade. Argue it if you disagree.

Either way the decision goes in DES-075's amendment. "What happens when durability cannot be confirmed after a successful write" is precisely what gets re-litigated in six months if it lives only in a code comment.

On your optional F4 ambiguity-warning: hold it. G1 may change what the ambiguity even is.
